messages:
Alex: Heads-up — enterprise asked for an "escape hatch" to pin traffic for a single org to a specific route/model via header. Want opinions on console UX, telemetry, and guardrails.
Maria: +1 on the request, but we need strong audit trail. every override must be logged with actor, reason, TTL.
Sasha: What's the exact semantics? Is this an allowlist that bypasses routing rules, or a sticky pin that expires?
Alex: Proposal: header-based override that sets a route key. It should be a time-limited pin (default 1h) and only available to orgs with the enterprise flag.
Kim: Also need RBAC on who can set it (admin vs svc account), and an API token scope. Otherwise this becomes a bypass for quotas.
Ryan: Telemetry: we should tag requests with override.reason and override.origin (console|api|support). That lets us roll up cost/latency per override.
Maria: +emoji :thumbsup: And surface a small panel in the console showing active pins for the org, with ability to revoke. Each entry shows created_by, created_at, ttl, reason, and audit link.
Sasha: Edge case: what if the pinned route is incompatible with model version (e.g., pinned to a dedicated-only route)? We need fallback policy.
Alex: Fallback default = normal routing ladder. But we should allow admin to set strict=true to fail fast. Show that in console.
Kim: Implementation sketch (header):
```
X-Redwood-Route-Override: org=acme;route=dedicated-us-west-2:gpu-a100;ttl=1h;reason=prod-incident;strict=false
```
Sasha: Nice. Also suggest we sign/verify the header when used by console/service to prevent forged headers from external clients.
devops-bot: note: there is an existing escape-hatch lambda that auto-creates sticky routes for internal tools — consider reusing audit pipeline.
Ryan: Metrics: create counters: override.created, override.revoked, override.expired. Add tags: org_id, created_by, origin. And a trace span `route.override.apply` to see latency impact.
Maria: UX: in rollouts page show a mini timeline when pins were active during a canary so PMs can correlate regressions. Also hint if the pin masked an outage.
Alex: Rollout plan: feature-flag the header acceptance and console UI. Canary to 5 enterprise orgs for 1 week, collect telemetry.
Kim: Security checklist: KMS-signed tokens for console requests, RBAC enforced in control plane, and audit -> immutable event stream forwarded to SIEM.
Sasha: Policy decision: denylist vs allowlist for which routes can be pinned. I vote allowlist per org plus global denylist for unsafe routes.
Alex: Agreed. We'll add an admin allowlist UI and default global denylist for internal-only routes.
Ryan: Quick thought: sampling of full request payloads when override applied (for 1% of requests) to help debugging without blowing logs.
Maria: Tasks: Alex -> API header proto + canary plan. Kim -> RBAC + signing design. Ryan -> telemetry schema + dashboards. Sasha -> allowlist/denylist policy doc. I'll wire console mockups.
Alex: Thanks. If no objections I'll create the ticket and spin up a RFC.
Sasha: No objections from me. :+1:
Kim: ok from security side, but will need 48h review window.
Ryan: Sounds good. I'll add alerting on override.revoked spikes.
Alex: Filing RFC now. will tag you all.
devops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary flag rollout at 2026-04-02T08:00Z (estimated).
